info.title: WCM API V3
info.description: REST API for Web Content Management. Provides CRUD operations for categories, libraries, site areas, and taxonomies with full OpenAPI 3.0 documentation. **IMPORTANT: To use this API Explorer, you must first log into the main DX Portal Web UI ([Portal Server](/wps/portal)) in a separate browser tab to establish an active LTPA session.** Your session timeout is enforced here.

put.description: Full-replace update (PUT) of a content item. 'name' is required. Omitting 'title', 'description', 'keywords', 'publishDate', or 'expiryDate' clears those fields. 'status' and 'language' are preserved when omitted. When 'elements' is provided the listed element values are replaced; omitting 'elements' leaves element values unchanged. Element format: each value is an object with 'type' (component type, e.g. TextComponent) and 'data.value' (the content value).

get.summary: Unified search across all WCM items
get.description:
Search for content, site areas, libraries, taxonomies, categories, and presentation templates in a single call. Supports two response modes:

**Summary mode** (default): Returns basic metadata only - id, type, name, title, description, path, lastModified, links

**Full mode** (includeMetadata=true): Returns complete data including all content elements, status, workflow, categories, profile, etc. This eliminates the N+1 query problem where search returns 30 items requiring 30 subsequent requests for full data.

**Field selection**: Use the 'fields' parameter to request specific fields only. Supports dot notation for nested fields (e.g., data.Body, data.Image).

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: This parameter is used to search item name, title, and description fields. Leave it empty to return all items. For example: article

parameters.name: libraryId
parameters.description: This parameter is used to query items that are linked to a specific library. Leave it empty to search across libraries. For example: db2e7d29-2dce-4f5a-9020-576ef1385884

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: This parameter is used to query items that are in a specific status. The following values can be used with this parameter: DRAFT, PUBLISHED, EXPIRED. For example: PUBLISHED

parameters.name: includeMetadata
parameters.description: This parameter is used to include full metadata in search results. Leave it empty or set it to false for summary results. Set it to true to include fields such as data, workflow, categories, profile, lock, history, authors, and owners.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: This parameter is used to return only specific fields in each search result. Leave it empty to return the default result shape. Dot notation can be used for nested fields.  For example: id,type,name,title,description,path,lastModified,links.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Zero-based offset for pagination. Use with 'limit'. Default: 0. Ignored if 'page' is provided.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of results per page. Default: 100. Overridden by 'pageSize' if provided.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Used with the pageSize parameter to define what set of results to display. For example: /search?pageSize=5&page=2

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: Used to restrict the number of items returned. Can be used with the page parameter to return specific pages. For example: /search?pageSize=5

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: This parameter is used to sort search results. Leave it empty for the default relevance/order. Supported fields: lastModified, created, name, title, type, score. Prefix the field with + for ascending or - for descending. For example: -lastModified

parameters.name: siteAreaId
parameters.description: This parameter is used to query items(Content and Site Area) that are linked to a specific site area. Leave it empty unless searching within one site area. For example: 7d5b0f04-7f87-4d44-9e06-8a5a39e99a71

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: Generic filter expression (reserved, not yet supported)
